result.title: Process then Retrieve: Investigating the Origins of the Modality Gap in Vision-Language Models
result.summary: Understanding the origins of the modality gap in vision language models remains a significant challenge. This work investigates whether differences in information density between modality specific tokens at the embedding layer contribute to this imbalance. We show that text tokens enter the model with much lower semantic density than visual tokens, driving early layers to focus on processing text representations before combining them with vision. Through mechanistic analysis, we demonstrate that replacing vision token positions with their semantically closest text token counterparts elicits increased attention to those positions in early layers. These findings provide a foundation for addressing the modality gap and provide insight to improve multimodal reasoning in VLM architectures.

AI.brief_summary: 该文从 embedding 层的信息密度差异入手，考察 VLM 模态差距的来源：文本 token 进入模型时语义密度远低于视觉 token，使早期层先处理文本表征、再与视觉结合；作者用机制分析替换视觉 token 位置为语义最近的文本 token，观察到早期层对相应位置的注意力上升。
AI.relevance_reason: 对 VLM 内部表征与模态融合顺序的诊断，可支撑「视觉旁路」与视觉证据是否被真正使用的问题，其中「早期层先处理文本再融合视觉」的结论可供核查 latent 推理中视觉信息被压缩或忽略的时机。
